Adding the technical checklist that our on-call runbook will expect from Acme's network team. I'll keep it short and deterministic so it can be handed to NOC: 

--- runbook excerpt (for network POC) ---
1) From a control-plane host (private subnet), curl the MTLS health endpoint:
   curl --cert /etc/redwood/certs/client.pem --key /etc/redwood/certs/client.key -v https://cp-api.local:8443/healthz
   Expected: 200 OK, json {"status":"ok","version":...} within 2s.
2) Verify TCP reachability from customer edge to each control-plane IP on 8443 (telnet/nc).
   nc -vz 10.10.5.12 8443
3) Check BGP next-hop acceptance: validate that the edge device has static routes pointing at the Redwood edge-facing interface.
4) Egress test: from a data-plane worker, do an outbound TLS handshake to our telemetry endpoint to ensure SNI passthrough + no interception:
   openssl s_client -connect redwood-telemetry.redwood.com:443 -servername redwood-telemetry.redwood.com
   Expected: certificate CN matches redwood-telemetry.redwood.com, verify chain valid.
5) Metrics verification: query Prometheus target on control-plane monitoring IP: http://10.10.10.4:9090/targets and confirm inference-node_* jobs are up.
6) KV cache warmup smoke: run a 10-request scripted workload (attached mini-script) against a single node and verify cache hit ratio increments in our dashboards within 5 minutes.
7) If control-plane is unreachable: verify NTP sync (chronyc sources), check iptables/firewall logs on the edge, and confirm that the MTLS cert thumbprint in KMS matches the one in /etc/redwood/certs.
--- end excerpt ---

I'll attach a tiny bash script we use for the KV warmup in the shared Drive. Also calling out cert rotation: Kimberly, can you confirm the planned rotation window? We prefer to rotate certs 48 hours after the canary if everything looks green.

-Jonas
